title: KoBold used AI to characterize the Mingomba copper deposit
summary: KoBold combined AI with geological expertise to characterize Mingomba; the sources do not isolate AI’s effect on discovery, costs, or environmental impact.
source_collection: University of Texas AI Opportunity Inventory
account: KoBold Africa chief executive Mfikeyi Makayi described work at Mingomba in a first-person account in PwC’s October 2024 Zambia mining report. She reported that data science helped the team target areas with substantial copper grade and thickness. The work combined historical exploration, drilling, geoscience, and computing. She also described decades of exploration before KoBold entered the project. The IEA later characterized the work as AI-assisted resource assessment. Neither account provides a controlled comparison or quantified AI-specific savings. Mingomba should not be presented as a deposit first discovered by AI.
purpose: The system supports geologists in choosing where to collect data and how to characterize mineral resources.
system: KoBold geological prediction and exploration systems
deployer: KoBold Metals and Mingomba Mining Limited
